gaps.gap: Graph-expansion provenance is not surfaced anywhere. A neighbour pulled in by graph_expand renders identically to a dense hit — no 'via CALLS from <seed>' note in the text body, no field in items[], nothing in meta. Internally the step knows seed qname, hop, edge kind, kind_weight and the decayed score, but _merge keeps only max(relevance) and throws the rest away.
gaps.why_it_hurts_the_next_call: The agent cannot tell 'this is the thing you asked for' from 'this calls the thing you asked for', so it either reads the neighbour as a false positive or misses the structural hint that a get_references(direction=callers) / get_context call on the seed would be the natural next step. The only residual signal (retriever_name is None on hydrated neighbours) is dropped before rendering.

notes:
Flow for kind=docs on the default route: SearchInput → build_search_query (pre_filter only) → chunk_search_graph.yaml: pre_filter → dense_fetcher (relevance = ANN score, retriever_name stamped by store) → metadata_post_filter → graph_expand (seeds = top-10 dense; 1-hop CALLS/INHERITS callers+callees; neighbours hydrated via uow.chunks.list, relevance = seed_sim*0.9, merged by max; sorted) → top_k_filter (k=50) → limit (8) → token_budget_formatter (2000 tokens; composite Chunk origin=composite_output, title=_composite). DocsSearch.search returns result (composite) + candidates (ranked ≤8). render_single_search collapses body via render_top_composite (items[0].text) and builds items[] from candidates. ToolRouter adds the zero-hit pointer+suggestion, ResponseEnvelope adds header/footer/meta and resolves `[[next:…]]` tokens.

Key precision points for the parent: (1) every hit's follow-up is get_symbol only; (2) provenance from graph_expand / centrality / community / rollup / RRF / multi-repo merge is computed then dropped before rendering — the cheapest Tier-0 lever is a scratch-key breadcrumb written by the steps and read by _chunk_piece; the cheapest Tier-1 lever is an additive meta key via the extras dict; (3) items[] already has path/start_line/end_line so a read_file pointer is derivable with zero new data; (4) the client `limit` is effectively dead against the YAML `limit: 8` cap and that cap records no truncation entry — that is a correctness/expectation bug worth flagging separately from the provenance work; (5) the `formatter:` param on token_budget_formatter is a vestigial registry hook — TokenBudgetStep.run never calls it. centrality_prior / community_diversity / parent_rollup are opt-in YAML steps and absent from all three shipped chunk presets, so 'surfacing' them requires enabling them first. Vendor-neutral; no competitor names or internal PR numbers used above (the source files themselves contain sub-PR references in comments, which were not repeated).

notes: Mechanics confirmed from source. (1) get_context closure: LookupTarget.parse → tree node → ReferenceService.context: forward CTE `find_transitive_callees` (cross-package, excludes 'similar' and unresolved `to_node_id IS NULL`, storage/sqlite/reference_store.py:147-180) up to `context.max_depth`; callees sorted (hop asc, pagerank desc, in_degree desc, qname); seed + top `limit-1`; hydrated from `uow.chunks.list(FieldIn(qualified_name…))` so `source_text` = chunk text (the only persisted content). Sources used: trees (resolution + focus row), references (walk), node_scores (ranking), chunks (text). NOT used: members, decisions. (2) 'Skeleton fidelity' = every node renders signature line + first docstring line; full bodies go only to 'central' nodes chosen by `_select_body_qnames` walking `_rank_context_nodes` order (pagerank if any node has it, else in_degree; closer hop breaks ties) under two bounds: cumulative chars <= body_ratio*token_budget*4 and count <= ceil(body_ratio*n). Non-body nodes get a `lookup-show:<qname>:source` pointer. 'full' render = hop-graded (hop0 source, hop1 signature, hop>=2 one line). Multi-target: ToolRouter._split_budget gives each card a 10% floor then proportional-by-closure-size share; floor degrades to even split above 10 cards. (3) get_symbol depths: summary/tree → PageIndex JSON of the node (summary=node only, tree=same JSON — both include nested `nodes`; _DEPTH_TO_SHOW maps summary→'default', tree→'tree', and both hit `_TREE_SHOWS` rendering the same `node.to_pageindex_json()`), items[] = pre-order outline rows; source → markdown header with path, fenced text capped at `symbol_source.max_lines`, inline `[… N more lines — read <path> directly]`, one items[] span row with kind recovered from the tree. (4) get_references per direction: callers = find_callers(to_node_id==target) ∪ cross edges_into; callees = find_callees(from) with unresolved rows substituted by matching cross edges; inherits = bases (from-side INHERITS) + subclasses (into ∪ exact to_name match, never bare-suffix) + cross; class-only, else InvalidArgumentError; impact = reverse CTE ranked (hop, -pagerank, -in_degree, qname) sliced to limit, federated across bundles by CrossRepoNavigator with a global visited set and `max_projects_per_walk`; governed_by = find_callers filtered to kind GOVERNS + cross GOVERNS edges. Rows are limit-sliced in LookupService before render; items[] mirror 1:1 with defining-node spans. (5) Unresolved edges: `to_node_id is None` rows render `⚠ from → to_name *(unresolved …)*`, sorted after resolved rows within each `## from <package>` group; lead line counts `(R resolved, U unresolved[, C cross-repo])`; items[] `to_qualified_name` = to_name, span null. impact/context CTEs drop unresolved edges entirely (no count surfaced). (6) All raised errors (NotFoundError with `[[next:search:…]]`, ServiceUnavailableError with YAML key) bypass the envelope — pointer tokens reach the client raw (documented at multi_project_search.py:462-467). Tier classification of the proposed fixes: every gap above has a Tier-0 (body text / pointer / description) remedy; only closure rows in get_context items[] or a real call-site line would be Tier 2.

notes:
Asymmetry verdict: the handoff graph is FILESYSTEM → FILESYSTEM (grep/glob → read_file → read_file continuation) and FILESYSTEM → search_codebase (fixed zero-hit suggestion), plus one accidental FILESYSTEM → INDEXED bridge (get_why accepts a path, via a naive path→qname rewrite). INDEXED → FILESYSTEM exists only as data (every indexed items[] row carries path+span; get_symbol(source) names the path in prose) but never as a rendered call — the pointer grammar has no read_file/grep action — and FILESYSTEM → SYMBOL tools (get_symbol/get_context/get_references) does not exist at all because grep/glob items lack qualified_name (ADR 0003 deferred the document_trees span-containment enrichment). So indexed tools point at each other; filesystem tools point at read_file; neither side points at the other by call.

Freshness semantics for mixing answers: the header/meta describe the INDEX snapshot (index_metadata.git_head vs live HEAD, TTL 5s, first project only). grep/glob/read_file always serve live disk regardless of index_stale, so `index_stale=true` on a grep response means 'the indexed tools may lag what you just read', not 'this grep is stale'. Uncommitted edits never flip the flag; the only per-file live fact is glob's mtime, and index_metadata.indexed_at is the comparison point nobody uses.

Tier classification of the candidate improvements: (a) per-hit `→ get_symbol(...)` pointer lines on grep/glob bodies, (b) `→ read_file(file_path=…, offset=…, limit=…)` pointers on indexed bodies / the symbol_source ledger entry (needs a new pointer action so next_pointers.enabled still governs it), (c) read_file trailer with in-window symbols + governing decisions, (d) `[modified after last index]` per-file annotation, (e) freshness line in the session-start pack — all Tier 0 (body/description/YAML). Mirroring any of them machine-readably (e.g. meta.enclosing_symbols, meta.file_modified_after_index) is Tier 1 via the extras→meta seam with an ADR, per the meta.resolution / meta.suggestion precedent. Adding qualified_name to grep items[] would be Tier 2. Implementation caveats: use the index (chunks.source_path / tree node.source_path == rel) for path→qname, not a string transform; dependency hits need dep_root re-basing because grep emits absolute dep paths; FileToolsService currently has no uow_factory (inject at build_sqlite_file_tools_service) and the chunk metadata schema does not admit source_path as a filter key, so a tree-store 'load by source_path' or an in-memory path→(package,module) map is the practical seam.

Summary of the routing spine: server.py handlers build the pydantic input (mcp_inputs.py) -> ToolRouter method -> per-project ProjectServices (search via MultiProjectSearch._search_body, symbol/refs/context via MultiProjectLookup._lookup_body/resolve_context, why/grep/glob/read_file/overview via _svc(project)) -> body triple (text, items, extras) -> ResponseEnvelope.wrap -> ToolResponse -> ENVELOPE_MODELS validation -> CallToolResult. Items are built in exactly five places: multi_project_search.py (_chunk_item/_member_item), lookup_service.py (_outline_item/_context_item/_reference_item), symbol_source.py (_span_item), decision_service.py (_decision_item/_why_item), file_tools.py (_span_item/_mtime_entries/_read_window), tool_router.py (_overview_items). Identifier contract in one line: node_id == qualified_name everywhere; code qnames are dotted identifier chains (addressable); doc/section qnames carry '#' fragments or hyphen/digit segments (unaddressable); decision identities are keys/ids nothing accepts; grep/glob/read_file speak only path+line. The only two places that translate between the path world and the qname world are LookupService._defining_span (qname -> path/span, read side) and DecisionService._path_to_qname (path -> module qname, get_why only, no line awareness). The most valuable Tier-0/Tier-1 levers without touching the frozen surface: (a) strip heading fragments in the search items[] row exactly as the body does (Tier 0? it changes a row VALUE not the field set — verify against contract §3.2 wording), (b) an additive meta field or body line naming the resolving project under recency fallback (Tier 1 precedent: meta.resolution/meta.suggestion), (c) a body pointer on grep content hits to the enclosing symbol (Tier 0, needs a path:line -> node lookup service over document_trees), (d) render the raw NotFoundError pointer through resolve_pointers before raising (Tier 0). Vendor-neutral, no internal PR numbers used.

notes: Mechanism summary. Renderers (formatting.py, symbol_source.py, decision_service.py, tool_router.py) emit SURFACE-NEUTRAL tokens `[[next:<action>:<target>[:<show>]]]` (actions: lookup, lookup-show, search, overview, why); ResponseEnvelope.wrap (envelope.py:82-103) opens a per-response ContextVar truncation ledger, runs produce(), then either resolve_pointers(body, surface) or strip_pointers(body), prepends the `[index: …]` header from the freshness probe, appends the `[truncated: N section(s) — recovery pointers inline]` footer (one line per ledger entry, recovery token resolved with the same surface/enabled rule), and assembles meta {tool, project, indexed_git_head, live_git_head, index_stale, truncated} + producer extras (resolution on get_references, suggestion on search/why/grep). Both surfaces share one envelope instance (server.py:497-512 for MCP with surface='mcp'; __main__.py:934-946 with surface='cli'; the CLI prints only `.text`, never items/meta — __main__.py:979-1120). resolve_pointers first runs a suppression pre-pass that deletes (token + EOL) any lookup / lookup-show token whose target fails is_symbol_target (mcp_inputs.py:65-77), then renders: lookup → get_symbol(target=…) | pydocs-mcp symbol X; lookup-show:{callers,callees,inherits,impact} → get_references(target, direction) | pydocs-mcp refs X --direction d; :context → get_context(targets=[X]) | pydocs-mcp context X; :tree/:source → get_symbol(target, depth=…) | pydocs-mcp symbol X --depth …; search → search_codebase(query=…) | pydocs-mcp search \"q\"; overview → get_overview() / get_overview(project=…) | pydocs-mcp overview [--project p]; why → get_why() / get_why(query=…) | pydocs-mcp why [\"q\"]. A lookup-show token with a missing/unknown show word is treated as indexed literal content and left verbatim (formatting.py:159-181). Target choice per producer: chunk hit → its qualified_name (heading `#slug` stripped); member → module.name; search elision → first non-empty qname across all hits; references full page → the queried target + same direction; context elision → the same target + 'context'; skeleton non-body node → that node + 'source'; overview module → module + 'context'; entry point / dependency / decision affected_qname → plain lookup; workspace project → overview:<name> (guarded by _PACKAGE_RE); package-doc cap → overview:<pkg>. Suppression/omission conditions: pointers_enabled=false (global strip, body+footer), target fails _TARGET_RE (silent drop), chunk without qualified_name, member missing module/name, entry name unsafe, ledger inactive (renderer called outside wrap → no record), decision affected list beyond 3. Suggestions (ADR 0007) are a separate mechanism: three fixed MCP-syntax strings under the `[suggestion:` prefix, per-rule YAML flags, mirrored to meta.suggestion, logged as JSON; grep rules append to body, the search/why rule reuses the overview pointer token as its body form. CLI/MCP inconsistencies observed: (1) suggestion text and read_file continuation note are MCP-syntax on both surfaces; (2) error messages carry raw tokens on both; (3) CLI pointers never carry --project even when the run is --workspace multi-repo; (4) the internal action vocabulary still says 'lookup'/'lookup-show' (the retired lookup tool) — harmless but a naming trap; (5) `overview:<pkg>` from package-doc truncation resolves to a project selector, not package=. Contract tiers as observed: text body, tool descriptions, YAML are Tier 0 (contract §1 lines 32-45); meta.resolution/meta.suggestion set the Tier-1 additive precedent (contract §2.2-2.3, ADR 0007 lines 66-78 record the four-step recipe and the pydantic extra=ignore pitfall); items[] field sets and params are Tier 2. Verification note: all claims are static reads; no server was run.
